title: Conformal Early-Stopping for Multimodal Reasoning Chains
research_question: Can conformal confidence sets over intermediate multimodal reasoning steps trigger reliable early stopping or evidence reacquisition in vision-language reasoning, reducing hallucinated chains without hurting final answer accuracy?
hypothesis: Applying conformal prediction to intermediate multimodal reasoning states will expose when a reasoning chain has become unreliable; using those signals to stop, revise, or reacquire visual evidence will improve calibration and reduce ungrounded reasoning compared with fixed-length multimodal chain-of-thought baselines.
motivation: The knowledge base surfaces a clear open problem around handling uncertainty and heterogeneous goals in adaptive systems, but recently rejected ideas show that directly reusing Bayesian or MAPE-K control for agent workflows is already crowded. A better gap is to transfer uncertainty-aware adaptation into multimodal reasoning, where long reasoning chains are often overconfident and hard to calibrate. Conformal prediction offers distribution-aware reliability signals, while the adaptive-control perspective suggests intervening at runtime rather than only scoring final answers. This creates a less-explored direction: confidence-triggered early stopping and evidence reacquisition for vision-language reasoning chains, which could improve trustworthiness and efficiency at the same time.
